_meta.adr: ADR-107 shillinq books and pipelinq originates the fee + ADR-037 modular register fragment + ADR-085 the checkout is a journey step — never edit shillinq_register.json
_meta.description: Competitor gap register row 1.11, online payment during intake. Declares FeeSchedule: what a case type costs, per intake channel of the owning app, valid between two dates. A fee is a council decision published in a verordening, so the schedule is configuration an administrator maintains and never a number in code. Where pipelinq is installed the fee originates as a product and the schedule references it (productRef); the schedule holds its own amount only when pipelinq is absent. payAtIntake decides what the intake journey does with the answer: required blocks completion until the payment is authorized, optional and later complete with a pending request and the link in the receipt. No PCI data: the money itself still moves through the PaymentRequest of case-payment-requests.

FeeSchedule.title: Fee Schedule
FeeSchedule.description: What a case type costs. One row per (targetApp, register, schema, typeProperty, typeValue, intakeChannel) and validity window, so a fee change is a new row with a new validFrom rather than an edit that loses what was charged last year. At most one schedule is valid per tuple on a given day: FeeScheduleService refuses an overlap and names the schedule it overlaps with, because two valid fees for one case type is a question nothing can answer. V0.2.0 (fees-payments-and-the-contract-register) makes the legal basis a structured citation and required, and moves the amount into `amounts`, one entry per intake channel with at most one default.

x-openregister-audit-trail.description: A fee is a council decision. Every create, edit and withdrawal is recorded on the OR audit-trail-immutable channel, so what was charged on a given day stays answerable.

targetApp.title: Target App
targetApp.description: The app whose objects this fee applies to, as its OpenRegister register slug names it. A fee is administered per case type of one app; shillinq never assumes there is only one.

register.title: Register
register.description: The register slug holding the objects that carry the fee.

schema.title: Schema
schema.description: The schema slug of those objects.

typeProperty.title: Type Property
typeProperty.description: The property on that schema holding the type value, so the same schedule shape works for a case type, a permit kind or a product line.

typeValue.title: Type Value
typeValue.description: The value of that property this fee applies to.

intakeChannel.title: Intake Channel
intakeChannel.description: Where the application came in. A counter and a website can charge differently, and a schedule with no channel is the default for every channel.

productRef.title: Product Ref
productRef.description: FK to the pipelinq product that originates this fee (ADR-107 decision 3). When set, the amount is READ from the product and the amount below is ignored, so the price lives in one place.

amount.title: Amount
amount.description: The fee when it does not differ per channel. Kept for the schedules written before `amounts` existed: a schedule with no `amounts` reads this as its default entry, which is the migration (REQ-FPCR-002). New schedules use `amounts`.

amounts.description: What the fee is, per intake channel. At most one entry omits intakeChannel and that entry is the default; a lookup takes the entry matching the case's channel and the default where none matches. A schedule with neither a matching channel nor a default is refused at save, because a fee that resolves to nothing looks exactly like a type that is free (REQ-FPCR-002).

intakeChannel.description: Where the application came in. Empty means this entry is the default.
intakeChannel.title: Intake Channel

amounts.title: Amounts

revenueAccount.title: Revenue Account
revenueAccount.description: The general-ledger account the receipt books against, overriding the requestType mapping for this type when set.

payAtIntake.title: Pay At Intake
payAtIntake.description: What the intake journey does with the fee. `required` blocks completion until the payment is authorized; `optional` completes with a pending request and offers the link; `later` completes and sends the link in the receipt.

legalBasis.description: The council decision this fee comes from: the regulation, the article inside it, and the date that article took effect. An amount that cannot say where it comes from cannot be checked by anyone, which is why a schedule without a basis is refused (REQ-FPCR-001).

regulation.description: The regulation the fee is published in.
regulation.title: Regulation

effectiveDate.description: The day that article took effect.
effectiveDate.title: Effective Date

legalBasis.title: Legal Basis

validFrom.title: Valid From
validFrom.description: First day this fee applies, inclusive.

validTo.title: Valid To
validTo.description: Last day this fee applies, inclusive. Empty means open ended.
